ns2:section.sectionText: Topic Section C1: Genre and Seriality In this seminar we will explore the evolution of detective, crime, ?hard-boiled,? and police procedural genres in short fiction, novels, novellas, film, and television series from the nineteenth century to the present day. Since most of these works appeared serially?appearing either in parts or as works in a series?our discussions will partly concern the effects of serial temporality (both within individual narratives and in the lived experience of readers and viewers). Crime genres also tend to generate a strong sense of region or place, whether nineteenth-century Paris or London, mid-century LA, Yorkshire in the 1970s, New York?s Korean immigrant communities, or contemporary Chicago, Denmark, or Bombay. Working at the intersection of genre, time, and place, we will consult a range of scholarly writing on these topics and keep a regular blog. Assignments will also include oral reports and a final paper.
